headline: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The project includes three wells, a storage tank, and a pipeline to the county water system.
meeting.recap: The project includes three wells, a storage tank, and a pipeline to the county water system.[[0:13:45]] The Department of Water Supply said it supports the bill because it helps DHHL house beneficiaries faster.[[0:15:00]] DHHL said its wait list has over 9,000 people, with an average age over 60.[[0:17:33]] DHHL said the three wells could produce about 1.728 million gallons a day, all for DHHL.[[0:19:26]] A councilmember asked why the county gets no water share, as in other DHHL projects.[[0:36:05]] A councilmember asked for language letting credits be adjusted if the wells produce more or less than estimated.[[0:55:37]] A five-minute recess was requested to address that question.[[0:56:01]]
meeting.next: DHHL said it would later share what percentage of the 9,000 on its wait list are from Maui. A five-minute recess was requested to address adding credit-adjustment language to the agreement.

trackerIssues.title: Three DHHL wells on Hawaiian Home Lands

issues.oneLine: DHHL wants the wells to speed up home building for its beneficiaries.
issues.why: DHHL said many people on its wait list pass away before receiving a home.
issues.next: DHHL said it would later share what percentage of its 9,000 wait-listers are from Maui.
issues.brief: DHHL said the full system could serve an estimated 2,880 residential units.[[#1]] DHHL said it formed a working group to get community feedback on the agreement.[[#2]] DHHL said the longer it waits to build homes, the more expensive they become for beneficiaries.[[#3]]
